newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Investment in Moscow may rise 40 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Investment in Moscow may rise 40 pct in 1997.

text.p: Russia's capital, Moscow, will see a 40 percent boom in investment this year, a senior city official said on Tuesday.
"By our forecasts, the rise will not exceed 40 percent on 1996 levels," First Deputy Mayor Iosif Ordzhonikidze told a signing ceremony for a major syndicated loan announced last month.
Investment in the Russian capital doubled in 1996 to $14.29 billion.

The loan -- a $200 million, three-year syndicated credit from 30 banks led by WestMerchant Bank, Societe Generale and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell -- is one of the biggest for any Eastern European or former Soviet city.
Ordzhonikidze said Moscow accounted for 66 percent of total investment in Russia last year.
Portfolio investment accounted for 44 percent of the total. He said that among strategic investors, food industry modernisation, construction and transport were the most popular.
He forecast growth in the leisure business and said the number of tourists to the capital would quadruple this year.
